â€‹### Why is it Important?

Senior leaders wanting to show their commitment to safety and learn about the safety issues in their own organization can do so by conducting regular walk-throughs for the sole purpose of discussing safety with the staff. Leadership walk-throughs provide an important opportunity for staff and leaders to reflect on their experiences with patient safety, and to discuss ideas for improvement. **Below are some tips for Conducting Effective Safety Walk Throughs:**

- Get a commitment from senior executives for an hour every week. Walk-throughs may be rescheduled but never canceled.

- Keep discussions focused on safety; don't dilute the safety message by trying to cover other topics.

- Involve all the senior executives in the organization, not just the chief executive officer.

- Communicate with managers so they understand why senior executives are visiting their departments.

- Make sure senior executives follow up and provide feedback to staff about issues raised during walk-throughs.

- Institute regular safety briefings. Pass along issues raised in the briefings (with names of the contributing staff members withheld) to the executives to talk about on their walk throughs.

- Prior to leaving the unit, have executives summarize the issues and ask staff to prioritize 2 to 3 items to be addressed.

- During these walk-throughs, communication should go two ways, with both the executives and the staff talking honestly and listening carefully. 

- Some organizations have found efforts where leaders 'walk through' and interact directly with staff especially effective in conjunction with conducting Safety Briefings, which can provide material for executives to start discussions.
